# causnet

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/USCbiostats/causnet/branch/master/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/USCbiostats/causnet?branch=master)
[![R build status](https://github.com/USCbiostats/causnet/workflows/R-CMD-check/badge.svg)](https://github.com/USCbiostats/causnet/actions)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of causnet is to find a globally optimal causal network given some data.

## Installation

You can install the development version from GitHub with:

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
require("devtools")
install_github("USCbiostats/causnet")
```


~You can install the released version of causnet from [CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org) with:~

``` r
install.packages("causnet")
```

## Example

```{r}
library(causnet)

# simulate data
set.seed(1234)
mydata <- simdat(n_var = 5)

# causnet results
links.s <- causnet(mydata)

links.s
```

### using BGE scoring function

To use the BGe scoring function, pass `score_bge()` to the `score_fun` argument.

```{r}
causnet(mydata, score_fun = score_bge)
```

### Candidate parents by stability selection

`causnet_stable()` replaces the p-value threshold `alpha` of `causnet()` with
stability selection (Meinshausen and Buhlmann, 2010). A variable is a candidate
parent if its selection frequency over `B` subsamples of half the observations
is at least `pi_thr`. The number of variables selected in each subsample is
derived from `tau`, a per-node bound on the per-family error rate (PFER) under
the assumptions of Theorem 1 of Meinshausen and Buhlmann (2010): the expected
number of falsely selected candidate parents of each node (each node is
screened as its own family of p - 1 candidates). Summed over the screened
nodes, the expected total number of falsely selected candidate parents (not
edges of the final network) is at most (number of screened nodes) x `tau`.
See `?causnet_stable` for the conditions of these bounds. Use `seed` for
reproducible subsamples.

```{r}
causnet_stable(mydata, tau = 1, pi_thr = 0.75, B = 100, seed = 1)
```

### Phenotype-driven search

`causnet()` and `causnet_stable()` can restrict the search to the neighbourhood
of an outcome variable. Give `outcome` as a column index or name: starting from
the outcome, candidate-parent links are followed for at most `n_levels` hops
(default 3), and the network is learned on the variables reached this way only.
With `outcome = NULL` (the default) the whole graph is searched. Here the search
only uses `V5` and its candidate parents:

```{r}
causnet(mydata, outcome = "V5", n_levels = 1)
```
